subject: Escrow hold & misapplied credits for NimbusCloud AWS marketplace invoices
messages:
From: billing@nimbuscloud.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:03:00Z
Subject: Notice: Escrow hold on AWS Marketplace invoices (PO 4632)

Hi Marissa,

We received an automated notification from AWS Marketplace that several of our September/October 2026 invoices were placed on escrow pending verification. Line items reference usage attributed to account 'redwood-inference-prod' and a PO mismatch (PO 4632 on our side, PO 4633 on the AWS feed). Our AP team put a stop on settlement until the discrepancy is cleared.

Could you confirm how Redwood is mapping the marketplace invoices to PO 4632? We need the mapping and any supporting metering exports to release funds; otherwise our payment will be delayed and AWS may apply late fees which will impact our reseller arrangement.

Attached: Nimbus_AWS_invoices_SEP-OCT_2026.pdf, PO_4632-Nimbus.pdf

Thanks,
Asha Mehta
Billing Manager, NimbusCloud
accounting@nimbuscloud.com
+1 415-555-0198

[Attachment: Nimbus_AWS_invoices_SEP-OCT_2026.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: billing@nimbuscloud.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T10:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Notice: Escrow hold on AWS Marketplace invoices (PO 4632)

Hi Asha — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: we appear to have two separate settlement entities set up in the marketplace listing and the AWS metering feed is being routed to the secondary entity (PO 4633) for a small subset of usage. That would explain the PO mismatch. Im looping in Marcus and Priya to pull the metering export and trace allocations back to the invoice rows.

What I'll deliver in the next 24 hours:
- A per-invoice row mapping (Redwood marketplace invoice line -> AWS charge id -> Nimbus PO)
- The raw metering export CSV for October usage
- Suggested journal/credit entries if Nimbus prefers a single settlement vs split entities

Marcus / Priya: Marcus, can you run the marketplace metering export and highlight the consumer account IDs linked to "redwood-inference-prod" between 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-31? Priya, please prepare a short note on whether the secondary settlement entity was activated for burst capacity during Oct 12-14 (we suspect an autoscale event).

Marissa
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: marketplace_metering_export_oct2026.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)]

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T15:37:00Z
Subject: FW: Escrow hold - metering export (internal)

Marissa — export attached and initial findings below.

Summary (preliminary):
- Metering export shows two marketplace seller-ids receiving usage: SLR-009 (primary) and SLR-019 (secondary). About 8% of billed tokens in Oct are under SLR-019.
- The SLR-019 rows carry an invoice_tag "PO:4633" in the AWS detail feed. On our side, the subscription/tenant was created under the primary seller but a migration script (2026-10-11) updated the tenant metadata and inadvertently pointed a subset of request routing to the secondary seller.
- Karthik: the migration was for a dedicated-capacity test; I will highlight exact timestamps so we can propose journal entries.

Next steps:
1) Karthik to confirm migration window and advise rollback vs journal.
2) Marissa to send this export and mapping to Nimbus so AP can match to their PO.
3) If Nimbus prefers, we can issue a credit for the amounts on SLR-019 and re-invoice under SLR-009.

[Attachment: marketplace_metering_export_oct2026.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)]

Marcus
Senior Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Escrow hold - metering export (internal)

Quick technical context: the migration script ran a scaled rollout on 2026-10-11 02:00 UTC to 2026-10-14 20:00 UTC. During the rollout we toggled a routing flag that inadvertently mapped certain long-run streaming sessions to the secondary seller (SLR-019). That explains the concentrated chunk of Oct usage.

I recommend we:
- Propose a journal/credit for the SLR-019 chargeable amount (~8% of Oct invoice) and re-issue an adjusted invoice under SLR-009 to Nimbus.
- If Nimbus insists on single-settlement, we can instead request AWS to reallocate the settlement entity for those charge IDs (AWS support ticket required) — that path takes longer but avoids manually issuing credits.

I'll prepare a concise rollback/migration timeline and the exact charge IDs by EOD so Marcus can calculate the monetary impact.

Karthik
Product Infra Lead (Serving Runtime)
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: billing@nimbuscloud.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: 2026-11-24T16:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Notice: Escrow hold on AWS Marketplace invoices (PO 4632) — proposed reconciliation

Hi Asha / Nimbus team,

Thanks for your patience — attached are the artifacts requested and our proposed reconciliation approach.

What we attached:
- marketplace_metering_export_oct2026.csv: rows flagged with seller_id SLR-019 include charge_id, timestamp, usage_units, and our internal tenant id.
- Nimbus_AWS_invoices_SEP-OCT_2026.pdf: annotated (inline comments) where SLR-019 usage maps to your invoice rows.
- PO_4632-Nimbus.pdf: we matched PO 4632 to the majority of rows; SLR-019 rows reference PO 4633 which caused the escrow hold.

Our recommendation (fastest path to release funds):
1) Redwood issues a single corrective credit memo equal to the SLR-019 billed amount for Oct 2026 and re-invoices Nimbus with the corrected PO (4632) references. This will allow Nimbus AP to apply the credit and make payment against the corrected invoice immediately.
2) Alternatively, if Nimbus prefers AWS-side reallocation, we are prepared to open the AWS ticket and coordinate; expect 7-14 business days for resolution which keeps funds in escrow until complete.

Estimated financial impact: ~$42,800 (8% of Oct invoice). Marcus will push formal numbers to your AP team in a separate CSV.

Please confirm which path you prefer and whether you need a Redwood-issued proforma or a DocuSign credit note.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0124

[Attachments: Nimbus_AWS_invoices_SEP-OCT_2026.pdf (PDF, 6 pages), marketplace_metering_export_oct2026.csv (CSV, 1.2MB), PO_4632-Nimbus.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]
